observation: A controlled crossover study (n=76: 38 ADHD adults, 38 neurotypical controls) found ADHD readers' comprehension improved ~7% under RSVP (word-by-word, no saccades) while controls' comprehension declined ~6% under the same condition, a statistically significant group×condition interaction (p=0.022).
claim: RSVP is a genuine, evidence-backed alternative reading mode for L3 specifically for ADHD readers, not a gimmick — but it should be opt-in and per-session since the same manipulation hurts neurotypical readers.
mechanism: RSVP removes the eye-movement/saccade demand specifically, which the crossover interaction shows helps ADHD readers and hurts controls — not a general pacing effect.
population: adults with ADHD (n=38, median age 23.3) vs. neurotypical controls (n=38)

implications.text: Offer an opt-in RSVP reading mode at L3, toggleable mid-passage without losing position, paired with the zoom dial's existing anchoring mechanic.

observation: Stern, Kolodny, Tsafrir, Cohen & Shalev (2024) found ADHD adults show significantly longer reading times and a distinct eye-movement signature (more regressions, reduced anticipatory pausing before predictable patterns) versus matched controls during uninterrupted text reading.
claim: L1's target read-time/word-count budget should not be calibrated from neurotypical reading-speed assumptions; it should be validated against Sam's own measured behavior.
mechanism: ADHD readers show a distinct reading signature (not just uniformly slower), including reduced predictive/top-down control during reading.
population: adults with ADHD vs. typically-developing adults
context: eye-tracking study, peer-reviewed but read via search synthesis (403 blocked)

implications.text: Calibrate L1's word-count/read-time target from Sam's own logged per-word reading time at each level, not a population reading-speed constant.

observation: A small (n=2) phenomenological study found ADHD adults report simultaneous text+audio (natural-voice TTS with word-level highlighting) as a scaffold that reduces cognitive load — the fixed narration pace prevented skimming/internal distraction — which appears to contradict Cognitive Load Theory's general redundancy-effect prediction that dual-channel same-content presentation costs comprehension, especially for complex syntax.
claim: The audio-as-scaffold-vs-audio-as-redundant-load tension is genuinely unresolved in the literature for ADHD readers and should be tested directly with Riemann's own instrumentation rather than assumed either way.
mechanism: Two plausible, opposing mechanisms (forced pacing preventing distraction vs. redundant-channel competition for the same cognitive resources) are both supported by adjacent evidence, with no study putting them head-to-head in an ADHD sample.
population: ADHD adults (n=2, self-selected from ADHD online communities)
context: phenomenological qualitative study, thematic analysis of journals/interviews

implications.text: Build synced-audio (word-highlighted, natural-voice TTS) as a first-class mode, but instrument dwell/comprehension data to let Sam's own usage settle the scaffold-vs-redundancy question.

observation: Dunlap et al. (1994, JABA) found letting ADHD/EBD students choose which task from a curated, equivalent menu (not whether to do it) increased on-task behavior and reduced disruptive behavior, with a yoked-control condition ruling out simple preference as the explanation; a 2025 qualitative study found ADHD students' open-ended self-directed pacing produced real costs (lost time, orientation energy) alongside valued autonomy.
claim: Bounded-menu choice ('start at L0, jump to a section, or let the dial pick') has real ADHD-specific supporting evidence; open-ended, unstructured self-navigation is where the cost documented in the 2025 study concentrates.
mechanism: Choice among a curated, low-navigation-cost menu carries independent value beyond preference, but unstructured self-regulation taxes the same executive processes ADHD impairs.
population: ADHD/EBD students (single-subject designs); ADHD students with inattentive-type presentation (2025 qualitative, n=2)
context: single-subject reversal/yoked-control design; qualitative interview study

implications.text: Give a small, bounded menu of starting points ('start at L0', 'jump to a section', 'let the dial pick') on opening a new document, rather than an open unstructured navigation space.

observation: A synthesis (Irrational Labs, citing a meta-analysis of 32 experiments) found progress bars that reveal high remaining effort reduce completion, stating an explicit time-to-complete reduces completion, and progress-bar placement before a task increases drop-off versus placement after.
claim: Riemann should never show a bare '% read' or 'time remaining' indicator as the primary framing of an in-progress document, and never place one before the content.
mechanism: Progress indicators that reveal high perceived remaining effort demotivate completion, an effect strongest when shown before rather than after a task begins.
population: general population (applied behavioral-science synthesis, meta-analytic backing for the core mechanism only)

implications.text: If a progress indicator exists at all, place it passively after/below content, avoid stating large remaining-time numbers, and consider 'endowed progress' framing (L0 done already counts).

observation: General (non-ADHD) research found the relationship between shame and procrastination is mediated by rumination, not a direct deterrent effect — shame triggers rumination that increases, not decreases, subsequent avoidance of the same task.
claim: Returning to unfinished content must be framed informationally ('here's where you left off'), never evaluatively ('here's what you didn't finish'), since self-critical framing is actively counterproductive, not neutral.
mechanism: Shame does not motivate completion; it triggers rumination that compounds avoidance of the very task it was meant to spur.
population: general adults (procrastination research); applied to ADHD by inference, not directly tested in an ADHD sample

implications.text: No red badges, no 'you have N unfinished items' language, no visual pile-up of abandoned documents; frame return-to-content as informational, not evaluative.

observation: A controlled neuropsychological study found adults with ADHD are significantly impaired on spatial working-memory tasks relative to controls, with the impairment increasing as task difficulty increases, and impairment specifically in strategy formation (not just raw capacity) for searching/encoding spatial information.
claim: A future spatial view should invest disproportionately in pre-built, consistent landmarks over emergent/self-organizing spatial structure, because the ADHD deficit is in strategy formation under difficulty, which gets worse as the space grows.
mechanism: The deficit is how-you-approach-the-problem, not just how-much-you-can-hold, so a spatial UI requiring the user to invent their own search/traversal strategy costs this population disproportionately more as scale increases.
population: adults diagnosed with ADHD (controlled neuropsychological study)

implications.text: Weight pre-built, consistent landmarks over emergent/self-organized spatial structure disproportionately as the abstraction-tree spatial view scales.

observation: A neurocomputational modeling study found unmedicated ADHD participants show an elevated 'novelty bonus' plus slower reward-value updating, jointly producing persistent selection of novel-but-suboptimal options even after repeated poor outcomes; methylphenidate selectively remediated this pattern.
claim: Novelty as an engagement lever is double-edged for ADHD users — the same mechanism that makes novelty an effective hook can trap users in low-value exploration loops, so novelty affordances must be paired with a fast, visible outcome signal.
mechanism: Elevated novelty valuation combined with slow reward-learning-rate updates means novel options keep getting chosen even when they're not paying off, unless the interface helps close the feedback loop the user's own reward learning is slow to close.
population: adults with ADHD, unmedicated vs. methylphenidate-treated (neuroimaging + computational modeling)

implications.text: Pair any novelty-driving affordance (new document type, surprising connection) with a fast, visible outcome/feedback signal rather than novelty alone.

observation: Safren et al.'s 2010 JAMA RCT found medicated adults with ADHD who added structured CBT (organization/planning, distractibility management, adaptive thinking) had ≥30% symptom reduction in over two-thirds of patients vs. one-third on relaxation training; broader meta-analytic synthesis found effect sizes drop substantially from waitlist control (g≈1.03) to active control (g≈0.32), meaning much of CBT's apparent benefit is generic structure/support, not CBT-specific technique.
claim: Externalized structure and scaffolding — not therapeutic technique or gamified motivation — is the transferable mechanism software can borrow from the strongest ADHD treatment evidence available.
mechanism: The active-control comparison shows most of CBT's benefit comes from consistent externalized structure and attention/support, which a well-designed tool can provide without replicating therapy technique.
population: medicated adults with ADHD (RCT and meta-analytic synthesis of 17-20 RCTs)

implications.text: Design any 'help me get unstuck' affordance around externalized structure (breaking things down, visible next step, check-ins), not motivational/gamified framing.
